issues.problem: The Title-Case-compound rule treats any capitalised previous word that is not in _FUNCTION_WORDS as a compound. Sentence-initial adverbs, prepositions and verbs therefore silence a genuine vendor right after them, and so does a vendor-qualified product name. Hit: 'Unlike Cursor, ...', 'Like Cursor', 'Install Cursor', 'Besides Director', 'Notably Director', 'Compare Director and cc10x'. Next-word cases are hit too: 'Melty Conductor' (the vendor's own name), 'Factory Droids', 'Cursor Pro', 'Director Pro', 'Cursor Composer', and lowercase head nouns such as 'Cursor agents' and 'Cursor model'. All of these counted at base. The real APO run is unaffected.

issues.suggested_fix: Ignore the previous word when it is itself sentence-initial (reuse _sentence_initial on its start), or when it is a known vendor or maker name such as Melty or Anysphere. Make the next-word compound test require that the pair is not a known product phrase, and drop the agent/agents/model head nouns or let them be overridden when the name is otherwise proper. Add these sentences to STILL_COUNTS.

issues.problem: The absence veto applies to the whole claim. Any 'no/zero/without/lacking/missing ... evidence|claims' anywhere in the claim drops every positive vote in it, including genuine ones in another clause. In this category 'without evidence' and 'missing evidence' also describe the evidence-gate feature itself. No genuine cell was lost on the real run, but the focus item said feature claims must not be hidden.
